Applying the new theory of analytic stacks of Clausen and Scholze we introduce a general notion of derived Tate adic spaces. We use this formalism to define the analytic de Rham stack in rigid geometry, extending the theory of $D$-cap-modules of Ardakov and Wadsley to the theory of analytic $D$-modules. We prove some foundational results such as the existence of a six functor formalism and Poincaré duality for analytic $D$-modules, generalizing previous work of Bode. Finally, we relate the theory of analytic $D$-modules to previous work of the author with Rodrigues Jacinto on solid locally analytic representations of $p$-adic Lie groups.

1. Introduction Motivation The main objective of this paper is to geometrically construct a six functor formalism for a suitable category of D D -modules over rigid spaces. To further develop this idea let us first recall some aspects of the classical theory of D D -modules. Let K K be a field of characteristic 0 0 and X X a smooth scheme over K K . Classically, the category of D D -modules over X X is constructed by first defining a ring of algebraic differential operators D X D_{X} over X X , and then taking the category of D X D_{X} -modules whose underlying 𝒪 X \mathscr{O}_{X} -module is quasi-coherent. If X X admits an étale map to an affine space X → 𝔸 K d X\to\mathbb{A}^{d}_{K} , then D X D_{X} can be explicitly constructed as the Weyl algebra D X = 𝒪 X [ ∂ T 1 , … , ∂ T d ] , D_{X}=\mathscr{O}_{X}[\partial_{T_{1}},\ldots,\partial_{T_{d}}], where 𝔸 K d = Spec ⁡ K ⁡ [ T 1 , … , T d ] \mathbb{A}^{d}_{K}=\Spec K[T_{1},\ldots,T_{d}] , and the variables ∂ T i \partial_{T_{i}} correspond to the partial derivations along the coordinate T i T_{i} . In [ Sim96 , ST97 ] , Simpson has proposed a different perspective on the theory of D D -modules by the employ of stacks. Let X X be a smooth variety over K K , Simpson attaches a space X d ​ R a ​ l ​ g X_{dR}^{alg} from commutative rings over K K to sets whose theory of quasi-coherent sheaves is naturally isomorphic to the theory of D D -modules over X X . More concretely, let Ring K \mathrm{Ring}_{K} be the category of commutative rings of finite type over K K , then Simpson’s de Rham stack is defined as the stack in the étale topology given by X d ​ R a ​ l ​ g ​ ( R ) = X ⁡ ( R red ) , X_{dR}^{alg}(R)=X(R^{\red}), where R red R^{\red} is the reduction of the ring R R . An advantage from this definition is that one can easily construct categories of D D -modules for any variety over K K without the smooth assumption, namely the previous formula for the de Rham stack extends to any stack over K K . The study of D D -modules via the de Rham stack, and its application to geometric Langlands, can be found in the work of Gaitsgory and Rozenblyum [ GR14 ] . Specializing to p p -adic geometry, let K K be a non-archimedean extension of ℚ p \mathbb{Q}_{p} and let X X be a smooth rigid space over K K . In the works [ AW18 , AW19 ] Ardakov and Wadsley have developed the theory of coadmissible 𝒟 wideparen \wideparen{\mathcal{D}} -modules over rigid spaces. The departure point to define the category of coadmissible 𝒟 wideparen \wideparen{\mathcal{D}} -modules is again a sheaf 𝒟 wideparen X \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X} of "infinite order p p -adic differential operators over X X ". To describe this sheaf, let us suppose for simplicity that X = Spa ⁡ A X=\Spa A is affinoid and that we have an étale map f : X → 𝔻 K d f:X\to\mathbb{D}^{d}_{K} to a polydisc 𝔻 K d = Spa ⁡ K ⁡ ⟨ T 1 , … , T d ⟩ \mathbb{D}^{d}_{K}=\Spa K\langle T_{1},\ldots,T_{d}\rangle . Then, as for schemes, we first consider the algebra of algebraic differential operators of X X : D X = A [ ∂ T 1 , … , ∂ T d ] . D_{X}=A[\partial_{T_{1}},\ldots,\partial_{T_{d}}]. The action of ∂ T i \partial_{T_{i}} on A A by derivations is continuous, so we can find N > 0 N>0 such that for all n ≥ N n\geq N the left sub- A ∘ A^{\circ} -module A ∘ [ p n ∂ T 1 , … , p n ∂ T d ] ⊂ D X A^{\circ}[p^{n}\partial_{T_{1}},\ldots,p^{n}\partial_{T_{d}}]\subset D_{X} is stable under multiplication. Thus, by taking p p -adic completions 𝒟 wideparen X ( n ) := A ⟨ p n ∂ T 1 , … , p n ∂ T d ⟩ \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X}^{(n)}:=A\langle p^{n}\partial_{T_{1}},\ldots,p^{n}\partial_{T_{d}}\rangle , and taking limits along n → ∞ n\to\infty , one constructs the algebra of infinite order differential operators 𝒟 wideparen X = lim ← n ⁡ 𝒟 wideparen X ( n ) . \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X}=\varprojlim_{n}\wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X}^{(n)}. The algebra 𝒟 wideparen X \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X} is known as a Fréchet-Stein algebra and its construction is motivated from the algebra of analytic distributions of p p -adic Lie groups of Schneider-Teitelbaum [ ST03 ] . In particular, there is a well defined category of coadmissible 𝒟 wideparen X \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X} -modules given by the limit along pullbacks of the categories of finite type 𝒟 wideparen X ( n ) \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X}^{(n)} -modules. Categories of coadmissible 𝒟 wideparen X \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X} -modules have been extended using bornological vector spaces, and a six functor formalism for 𝒟 wideparen X \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X} -modules has been constructed by Bode in [ Bod21 ] . The theory of the analytic de Rham stack developed in this work is then a conciliation between the geometric theory of D D -modules of Simpson via the de Rham stack, and the theory of 𝒟 wideparen X \wideparen{\mathcal{D}}_{X} -modules of Ardakov and Wadsley. To justify the tools used to construct the analytic de Rham stack let us start with an example. Let K K be a field of characteristic 0 0 , and let 𝔾 a = Spec ⁡ K ⁡ [ T ] \mathbb{G}_{a}=\Spec K[T] be an affine space over K K seen as an additive group. It follows from the definition of the algebraic de Rham stack that 𝔾 a , d ​ R a ​ l ​ g = 𝔾 a / 𝔾 ^ a \mathbb{G}_{a,dR}^{alg}=\mathbb{G}_{a}/\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{a} where 𝔾 ^ a \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{a} is the formal completion at 0 ∈ 𝔾 a 0\in\mathbb{G}_{a} , acting by translations. It turns out that the Cartier dual of the stack ∗ / 𝔾 ^ a */\widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{a} is just 𝔾 a \mathbb{G}_{a} , then, it is expected (and indeed the case) that modules over 𝔾 a , d ​ R a ​ l ​ g \mathbb{G}_{a,dR}^{alg} are given by sheaves on 𝔾 a \mathbb{G}_{a} together with an operator ∂ T \partial_{T} (Cartier dual of ∗ / 𝔾 a ^ */\widehat{\mathbb{G}_{a}} ), that is equivariant with respect to the module structure on 𝔾 a \mathbb{G}_{a} via the additive action of 𝔾 ^ a \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{a} on 𝔾 a \mathbb{G}_{a} (i.e. that ∂ T \partial_{T} acts by derivations). Let us now take K / ℚ p K/\mathbb{Q}_{p} a non-achimedean extension, and let 𝔾 a = 𝔻 K 1 = Spa ⁡ K ⁡ ⟨ T ⟩ \mathbb{G}_{a}=\mathbb{D}^{1}_{K}=\Spa K\langle T\rangle be the open affinoid disc seen as an additive group. We would like to define an analytic de Rham stack 𝔾 a , d ​ R \mathbb{G}_{a,dR} whose theory of quasi-coherent sheaves is related to the theory of 𝒟 wideparen \wideparen{\mathcal{D}} -modules. By construction, the sheaf 𝒟 wideparen \wideparen{\mathcal{D}} of infinite order p p -adic differential operators has cotangent variables (i.e. the derivations ∂ T \partial_{T} ) that look like global sections of an analytic affine space 𝔸 K 1 , an \mathbb{A}^{1,\an}_{K} . Moreover, the category of coadmissible 𝒟 wideparen \wideparen{\mathcal{D}} -modules is a non-commutative analogue of the category of coherent sheaves on a relative analytic affine space (eg. 𝔸 K 1 , an \mathbb{A}^{1,\an}_{K} ). Therefore, we would like to define the analytic de Rham stack in such a way that 𝔾 a , d ​ R = 𝔾 a / 𝔾 a † , \mathbb{G}_{a,dR}=\mathbb{G}_{a}/\mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger}, with 𝔾 a † ⊂ 𝔾 a \mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger}\subset\mathbb{G}_{a} a subgroup acting by translations, and such that ∗ / 𝔾 a † */\mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger} is the Cartier dual of 𝔸 K 1 , an \mathbb{A}^{1,\an}_{K} (in a suitable sense). It is known that the continuous dual of 𝒪 ⁡ ( 𝔸 K 1 , an ) \mathscr{O}(\mathbb{A}^{1,\an}_{K}) is given, as a Hopf algebra, by the ring of germs of functions at 0 ∈ 𝔾 a 0\in\mathbb{G}_{a} K ​ { T } † = lim → n ⁡ K ⁡ ⟨ T p n ⟩ . K\{T\}^{\dagger}=\varinjlim_{n}K\langle\frac{T}{p^{n}}\rangle. Therefore, a reasonable candidate for 𝔾 a † \mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger} would be given by 𝔾 a † = Spa ⁡ K ​ { T } † . \mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger}=\Spa K\{T\}^{\dagger}. Here is where several foundational problems appear. First, we are obligated to work with topological rings, and in order to have a good theory of analytic D D -modules as quasi-coherent sheaves of a stack, we also need to work with topological modules. This problem is solved thanks to the theory of analytic geometry and condensed mathematics of Clausen and Scholze [ CS19 , CS20 , CS22 ] . Second, if we ever expect to built up a six functor formalism of analytic D D -modules from the theory of complete modules of analytic rings, we need to construct categories of analytic stacks, and have a strong descent theory. Again, analytic geometry comes to the rescue, this time making use of the abstract theory of six functor formalisms and 𝒟 \mathscr{D} -stacks as in [ Man22b , Man22a ] and [ Sch23 ] . Once we have analytic stacks and complete modules at our disposal, we can make sense to objects such as 𝔾 a / 𝔾 a † \mathbb{G}_{a}/\mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger} , as well as to its category of complete modules. However, in order to make a good definition of the analytic de Rham stack, we would need to mimic Simpson’s construction of the algebraic de Rham stack. The key idea is that, while the space 𝔾 ^ a \widehat{\mathbb{G}}_{a} represents the nilradical of a discrete ring R R (i.e. those elements a a such that a n = 0 a^{n}=0 for some n n ), the space 𝔾 a † \mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger} represents a " † \dagger -nilradical" for a suitable category of analytic rings R R . In other words, 𝔾 a † \mathbb{G}_{a}^{\dagger} represents elements a ∈ R a\in R "of spectral norm zero", i.e. such that | a | ≤ | p n | |a|\leq|p^{n}| for all n ≥ 0 n\geq 0 . Thus, our first step is to restrict the theory of analytic rings to a theory of "bounded affinoid rings" R R for which we can construct a † \dagger -nilradical Nil † ⁡ ( R ) \Nil^{\dagger}(R) . Another motivation for the introduction of bounded affinoid rings arises from Tate algebras: we should only expect to construct an analytic de Rham stack for rings that look like affinoid Tate algebras, namely, for rings admitting a pseudo-uniformizer in a suitable sense. After bounded affinoid rings are introduced, we study some fundamental geometric properties of them in Sections 2 and 3 : an analytic topology analogue to the analytic topology of adic spaces; a theory of derived Tate adic spaces obtained by gluing bounded affinoid rings via rational localizations; the theory of the cotangent complex of analytic rings; different notions of morphisms of finite presentation appearing in non-archimedean analytic geometry; a deformation theoretic description of smooth maps of morphisms of (solid) finite presentation of derived Tate adic spaces; Serre duality; a new deformation condition involving † \dagger -nilradicals. This study on derived rigid geometry settles the basis for the theory of the analytic the Rham stack. Finally, once all the prerequisites in derived rigid geometry are done, we can start the study of the analytic de Rham stack. Let X X be a rigid space over ℚ p \mathbb{Q}_{p} , and let Aff ℚ p b \Aff_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}^{b} be the ( ∞ \infty -)category of bounded affinoid rings over ℚ p \mathbb{Q}_{p} , then the analytic de Rham stack X d ​ R X_{dR} will be defined as a suitable sheafification of the prestack mapping 𝒜 ∈ Aff ℚ p b \mathcal{A}\in\Aff_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}^{b} to X d ​ R ( 𝒜 ) = X ( 𝒜 † − red ) , X_{dR}(\mathcal{A})=X(\mathcal{A}^{\dagger-\red}), where 𝒜 † − red := 𝒜 / Nil † ( 𝒜 ) \mathcal{A}^{\dagger-\red}:=\mathcal{A}/\Nil^{\dagger}(\mathcal{A}) is the " † \dagger -reduction of 𝒜 \mathcal{A} ". Our workhorse to prove properties on the analytic de Rham stack, such as the existence of six functors, Poincaré duality, and the construction of the Hodge filtration, will be a new theory of Cartier duality for analytic vector bundles over derived Tate adic spaces in Section 4 . The main theory of the analytic de Rham stack, in particular the construction of six functors for analytic D D -modules, is the content of Section 5 . We finish the paper with a generalization of the analytic de Rham stack of smooth morphisms in the equivariant setting in Section 6 , obtaining a generalization of equivariant 𝒟 wideparen \wideparen{\mathcal{D}} -modules of Ardakov [ Ard21 ] , and of the theory of solid locally analytic representations of p p -adic Lie groups of [ RJRC22 , RJRC23 ] . Overview of the paper The body of the paper is divided in two main parts. First, we develop the theory of derived Tate adic spaces and Tate stacks in Sections 2 and 3 . The second part consists on Sections 4 , 5 and 6 , where we study different incarnations of Cartier duality of vector bundles, we define the analytic de Rham stack for Tate stacks over ℚ p \mathbb{Q}_{p} , and finally we relate the theory of the analytic de Rham stack with the theory of locally analytic representations of p p -adic Lie groups. § 2 Derived Tate adic spaces The theory of adic spaces of Huber [ Hub94 ] have been the language for non-archimedean analytic geometry in the last few decades, a weakness of this category are the restrictions imposed in the definition of complete Huber pairs. The main goal of this section is the introduction of the ∞ \infty -category of bounded affinoid rings (Definition 2.6.10 ), generalizing the category of Tate Huber pairs, over which we can do both analytic and derived algebraic geometry. Similarly as for Huber pairs, one can construct a spectral space Spa ⁡ 𝒜 \Spa\mathcal{A} for any bounded affinoid ring 𝒜 \mathcal{A} (Definition 2.7.3 ), generalizing the adic spectrum of an Huber ring. Maps between bounded affinoid rings will give rise to spectral maps of the adic spectra, and solid quasi-coherent modules will satisfy descent for the analytic topology. A bounded affinoid ring has the feature that any function is bounded in the sense of the theorem down below. Moreover, one can define condensed and † \dagger -nilradicals for these rings, consisting on ideals of uniformly nilpotent or overconvergently close to zero elements respectively. Definition 1.0.2 . We let Aff R b \Aff^{b}_{R} denote be the opposite category of bounded affinoid rings, an object in Aff R b \Aff^{b}_{R} is called a bounded affinoid space . Given 𝒜 \mathcal{A} a bounded affinoid ring we let AnSpec ⁡ 𝒜 ∈ Aff R b \AnSpec\mathcal{A}\in\Aff^{b}_{R} be its analytic spectrum . We let AdicSp R \AdicSp_{R} denote the ∞ \infty -category of derived Tate adic spaces over R R . The previous definition of derived Tate adic spaces is an extension of Huber’s analytic adic spaces. The choice of the analytic topology to glue bounded affinoid rings is an arbitrary choice that was taken to compare with the classical theory. We will see in § 3 that one can still do geometry in different kind of Grothendieck topologies, as long as one has descent for the six functor formalism of quasi-coherent sheaves. § 3 Tate stacks In this section we continue developing the theory of derived Tate adic spaces. In § 3.1 we recall some language in the theory of abstract six functor formalisms of [ Man22b , Man22a ] and [ Sch23 ] . Then in § 3.2 , we use [ Sch23 , Theorem 4.20] to construct a very large six functor formalism on a category of analytic 𝒟 \mathscr{D} -stacks on bounded affinoid rings (Definitions 3.2.7 and 3.2.10 ). We define different notions of morphisms of finite presentations in analytic rings in § 3.3 , study basic properties of cotangent complexes in analytic rings in § 3.4 , and introduce the notion of solid smooth and étale maps of derived Tate adic spaces in § 3.5 . We obtain an equivalent description of solid smooth and étale maps as formally smooth and étale maps of solid finite presentation (Theorem 3.5.6 and Corollary 3.5.16 ). Theorem 1.0.3 . Let f : X → Y f:X\to Y be a morphism of solid finite presentation of derived Tate adic spaces over R = ℤ ⁡ ( ( π ) ) R=\mathbb{Z}((\pi)) . The following are equivalent: (1) The map f f is formally smooth (resp. étale). (2) The map f f is solid smooth (resp. étale), namely, locally in the analytic topology of X X and Y Y the map f f is standard solid smooth (resp. standard solid étale). Let f : X → Y f:X\to Y be a solid smooth (resp étale) map of derived Tate adic spaces over R R . Then f f is † \dagger -formally smooth (resp. étale) locally in the analytic topology of X X and Y Y . In the next sections we apply all the previous theory on derived rigid geometry to study Cartier duality of vector bundles, and to construct a six functor formalism for analytic D D -modules. § 4 Cartier duality for vector bundles With the introduction of derived Tate adic spaces, new commutative group objects appear in the nature making possible new incarnations of Cartier duality. In this section we do not pretend to give a definition or an abstract set up for a Cartier duality theorem, instead we explore new examples of Cartier duality arising from analytic subspaces of vector bundles. For technical reasons, these Cartier duality isomorphisms are easier to describe if we restrict ourselves to analytic geometry over ℚ p \mathbb{Q}_{p} , for simplicity let us even restrict ourselves to derived Tate adic spaces over ℚ p \mathbb{Q}_{p} .
